cards.title: Borrowed Authority
cards.instruction: Project confident authority while quietly working to keep everyone cooperative. Your confidence depends on their cooperation.

cards.title: You Handle the Evidence
cards.instruction: Make someone else take responsibility for the evidence, loose end, or difficult follow-up.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: We'll close the raffle accounts today. Explain my missing magician's receipt to the treasurer; you booked him.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: You paid him. I only found his number.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Then you've got the number. I'll send the payment date; get us a replacement.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I already rang. He needs the treasurer to email him directly.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Draft her email. I'll get her to send it; copy yourself in so you can chase the reply.

cardFidelity.evidence: A1 directs closing accounts and assigns explanation; A3 supplies payment date after B corrects responsibility; A5 coordinates treasurer sending but makes B draft and chase the reply.

responseLogic.evidence: B2 only found number corrects A1 booked claim; B4 explicitly already rang, establishing the source of the direct-email requirement without an imagined call between turns.

relationship.evidence: B2 resists inaccurate responsibility and B4 reports completed effort plus the actual next constraint.

heightening.evidence: B4 direct-treasurer requirement causes A5 a new division of work that still leaves the loose end with B.

specificity.evidence: A1 raffle, magician receipt and treasurer establish the evidence problem; later turns specify the retrieval route.

brevityWit.evidence: A5 draft, sending coordination and copied follow-up are distinct tasks in one causal process, not a pile of unrelated demands.
